text: The planet's name references Stanisław Lem's novel Solaris; the world itself is loosely modelled on Earth as the third planet of its system.
quote: 星球名字参考了 斯坦尼斯瓦夫·莱姆的《Solaris》翻译为（索拉里斯星）的同名小说
source: GameKee 鸣潮wiki · 世界观文化考据 (repost of 库街区 article by 結星)

text: A Huanglong moon festival for family reunions and wishes, with a moon-fox origin tale: the Mid-Autumn Festival, with its reunions, moon-gazing and the Chang'e and Jade Rabbit legends.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: Jinzhou's Liondance blends martial arts and dance and is performed at festivals and before battles, as the Chinese lion dance is, which also grew out of martial-arts schools.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: "Loong" is the romanisation used for the Chinese dragon (龙, lóng) to set it apart from the Western dragon; Jué's serpentine, water-and-weather Loong follows that tradition.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: Ragunna crowns the Carnevale's finest performer with the "Laurel", the Greco-Roman wreath given to victors, poets and champions.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: The Blessed Maiden's name is the fleur-de-lis, the stylised lily of French royalty and a Marian symbol of purity, fitting a saintly vessel of the Sentinel.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: Galbrena's Chimera is named after the Greek Chimera, the fire-breathing hybrid of lion, goat and serpent.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: Abby's other name, Abraxas, is a figure from Gnostic tradition: a deity beyond good and evil whose name adds up to 365, later read by Hermann Hesse and Carl Jung as uniting opposites.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: Ashinohara's Japanese-styled shrine maidens follow the miko of Shinto shrines; Hiyuki's Legacy Talisman, the Suzu, is the bell miko use in ritual dance.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: The Séance Society promises contact with dead loved ones, like the spiritualist séance.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: The wiki describes the Stridergate as a connective wormhole believed to lead to outer space, the Einstein–Rosen bridge of physics and science fiction.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: One of nine interstellar probes launched before the Etheric Sea closed, still recording signals: the Voyager probes, humanity's farthest emissaries, which also carry a message for whoever finds them.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: A Resonator who pushes their Resonance beyond its rated limit loses control, the same term as running a processor past its rated clock speed, with the same risk of burning out.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: A sword-bearing maiden revered as a saint, credited with saving her land and martyred for it; the Blessed Maiden's arc echoes the Maid of Orléans. A loose parallel.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: Haultir, the Blessed Maiden's "Sword of Virtue", sounds like Hauteclere, the sword of the paladin Oliver in The Song of Roland. A loose parallel by name.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)

text: Nameless knights who end up keeping windmills, and not for the reason it seems, recall Don Quixote, the would-be knight who tilts at windmills. A loose parallel.
source: Echo Codex analysis (not stated by a source)
